title: DECOR: Degree-Corrected Social Graph Refinement for Fake News Detection

problem.claim: Fake news detection using graph neural networks is limited by noisy or suboptimal social graph structures.

gap.claim: Existing graph structure learning methods can be computationally expensive because they use node features to update edge weights, limiting applicability to large-scale social graphs.

contributions.claim: DECOR applies Degree-Corrected Stochastic Blockmodels to fake news detection.
DECOR uses a lightweight refinement component that iteratively updates edge weights through a learnable degree correction mask jointly optimized with a GNN-based detector.
News article node degrees exhibit patterns indicative of news veracity.

stated_novelty.claim: The work presents a novel approach to social graph refinement for fake news detection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two real-world benchmarks reportedly validate DECOR's effectiveness and efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph neural networks are increasingly used to exploit social context for fake news detection.
Fixed and noisy graph structures can limit GNN expressiveness, while existing refinement methods may be too expensive for large-scale graphs.
News article node degrees show patterns associated with news veracity.
DECOR combines degree-corrected stochastic blockmodels with lightweight iterative edge-weight refinement and joint GNN optimization.
The authors report effectiveness and efficiency on two real-world benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: Node-degree patterns may contain information about news veracity.

interpretation.claim: Structural graph statistics can serve as useful signals for graph-based classification.

application.claim: When graph edges are noisy, examine degree distributions or other structural statistics before relying only on node features.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that degree patterns generalize beyond the reported fake news detection setting.

source_observation.claim: A learnable degree correction mask can iteratively update edge weights with a GNN detector.

interpretation.claim: Lightweight structure refinement may reduce the computational burden of feature-driven graph structure learning.

application.claim: For large social graphs, consider jointly optimizing a compact structural correction module with the downstream detector.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide computational complexity, scalability thresholds, or comparative efficiency measurements.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two benchmarks, datasets, baselines, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not quantify effectiveness, efficiency, computational cost, or improvements.
The abstract does not describe the degree-correction mask architecture, optimization details, or ablation results.
